title: We tested Instinct, Muse and Grokbot. They’re ridiculous.

speakers.name: Sam Parr (inferred from channel; owns Hampton per L731; not named in transcript)
Shaan Puri (inferred from channel; not named in transcript)

promo_conflict: One host has a Micro One affiliate link and says he would earn fees from referrals (L737-L746). A host says he invests in SF Compute (L1140). AI companies are named as heavy advertisers on creator channels (L697, L705).

stated_problem.quote: Now everybody in the world is going to have access to things that only rich people used to have before.

idea.name: Instinct – AI personal assistant over iMessage
idea.one_liner: A consumer AI assistant you text like a person. It books, buys, chases customer service and plans events, is free to use, and takes a cut of the purchases it makes for users.
idea.offer: A personal assistant over iMessage that handles errands, bookings, purchases and disputes
idea.revenue_model: Free forever; a take rate on transactions it makes for users

key_quotes.quote: Instinct is something that's just in your I message.
And he wants to make his money taking a cut on all the transactions.
And so it starts harassing them.
So for example, just saying it's a personal assistant instead of saying it's an AI agent.

claims.claim: Valued at $10B about two months after launch
claims.quote: And it's now valued at $10 billion.

claims.claim: Raised at a $2.5B valuation three weeks earlier
claims.quote: They raised around at two and a half billion three weeks ago.

claims.claim: Founder says usage grows 10% per day, compounding
claims.quote: The guy, the founder said they're growing 10% compounding daily.

claims.claim: Over $1B of transactions while still invite-only
claims.quote: He said that already while they're in invite only, they've already crossed a billion dollars of transactions.

claims.claim: 40-50% of transaction volume is travel
claims.quote: That 40 or 50% of that was travel.

claims.claim: 40% of users hand over a credit card within three weeks
claims.quote: he said that 40% of users give instinct their credit card within the first three weeks.

claims.claim: 80% retention among users who saved a card
claims.quote: And then once they've done that, there's like an 80% retention rate,

acquisition_channels.details: Invite-only access spread by word of mouth; the host was invited and got his wife using it
Founder's first podcast interview (Invest Like the Best); a minimal landing page where you enter your phone number

ideas.delivery: Fully software. An AI agent works through iMessage text, sends emails, books services, buys with a stored card and connects to the user's inbox and accounts.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR (access to inboxes and financial accounts), PSRs/FCA if it handles payments, and consumer-protection rules on agents buying for users

stated_problem.quote: it just works for people that they don't have to know how to do all the, the underlying setup and training and maintenance and all that

idea.name: Muse – Meta's hosted personal agent
idea.one_liner: Meta's own-app AI assistant. It runs an OpenClaw-style agent for each user in a cloud sandbox, so nobody has to set it up.
idea.offer: A personal AI agent app with a sandboxed cloud machine per user
idea.revenue_model: Not stated (strategic: owning the agent layer and transaction gateway)

key_quotes.quote: It literally is the kind of open clause setup, but just done in the cloud where you don't have to do any of that setup.
Muse is a lot like instinct, but it's snappy or it's faster.
Amazon shut off access to muse to be able to go buy stuff on Amazon.

claims.claim: Meta stock rose 24% in a month on the back of Muse
claims.quote: And in the last month, meta stock prices up 24% off the back of this.

claims.claim: Roughly $500B added to market cap
claims.quote: It's like basically they added like $500 billion in market cap.

acquisition_channels.details: Predicted heavy sponsorship of Instagram creators and podcasts (L586)

ideas.delivery: Meta's own app, backed by one sandboxed machine per user in Meta's server farms

idea.name: Grokbot – Slack-style multi-bot assistant
idea.one_liner: xAI's assistant, where a user creates separate bots with single jobs (tax, health, social media), each with its own goal and instructions.

key_quotes.quote: So Grockbot is very much like Slack.
Hey, tax guy, your job is to be constantly on top of my tax situation
Grockbach feels slow and heavy compared to this.

acquisition_channels.details: Early access through Elon's xAI ecosystem

ideas.delivery: Software agents configured by the user with a goal and instructions
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR (health and tax data is special-category/sensitive)

stated_problem.quote: Yeah, all the, all the models so far have been trained on the open internet.

idea.name: Micro One – private company data broker for AI labs
idea.one_liner: Pays private companies for their internal data (Notion, Slack, Gmail, Drive) and resells it to frontier LLM labs as training data, keeping a margin.
idea.customer: Frontier AI labs (buyers) and privately held companies (suppliers)
idea.offer: Buys non-public business data plus expert human data and evaluations
idea.revenue_model: Data resale margin (example: lab pays ~$1M, company gets ~$600-800K)

key_quotes.quote: if you plug in your notion, your slack, your Gmail, your drive and a bunch of other information.
Their business model is that they want all types of data that people that aren't available to the public and they sell it to the large.
Micro run micro one is a data lab to train frontier models.

claims.claim: Reached about $1B run rate in eight months
claims.quote: they grew to something like a billion dollars in run rate in a matter of eight months.

claims.claim: Offered the host's company $800K for its data
claims.quote: They offered us $800,000 for our data.

claims.claim: $50K affiliate fee per referred company
claims.quote: We'll give you $50,000 for everyone you refer to us.

claims.claim: 80 people went through the host's affiliate flow
claims.quote: I think we had 80 people go through that flow.

claims.claim: If eight convert, the host gets about $300K in affiliate fees (maths is off: 8 × $50K = $400K)
claims.quote: let's just say that eight convert, that's a, I can't even do that math, $300,000 that they will give me an affiliate fees.

claims.claim: Labs might pay about $1M per dataset
claims.quote: they will pay let's say a million dollars for it.

acquisition_channels.details: Big affiliate fees ($50K per referral) paid to creators and founders
Direct offers to privately held companies

ideas.delivery: Companies connect their workspace tools; Micro One packages the data and sells it to LLM labs; also pays experts for human data and evaluations
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR: selling internal comms that contain employee and customer personal data needs a lawful basis and transparency. Also confidentiality and trade-secret obligations.

idea.name: Small creators running AI-company sponsorships
idea.one_liner: Solo Instagram and YouTube creators with under 100K followers who earn $1M+ a year mostly from AI companies' ad and affiliate budgets.
idea.customer: AI companies buying ads and affiliate placements
idea.offer: Sponsored talking-head clips and podcast clips

key_quotes.quote: I'm just holding up their phone talking.
it's just crazy how much money the AI industry has to buy ads.

claims.claim: These creators each have under 100K followers
claims.quote: All of the people who I've talked to have less than a hundred thousand followers

claims.claim: Each makes over $1M a year in ad revenue, mostly from AI companies
claims.quote: And all of them that I talked to are doing over a million dollars a year and add revenue, almost entirely from AI companies.

claims.claim: Three solo creators (with part-time help) make over $10M a year
claims.quote: And they are doing over 10 million dollars a year in revenue.

claims.claim: Sponsored products range from $2K/month up to $50K affiliate fees
claims.quote: the product costs two thousand a month all the way up to like the micro one where they're giving like, you know, $50,000 affiliate fees.

ideas.delivery: The creator records on camera; a part-time VA helps
ideas.other_uk_rules: ASA/CAP Code and CMA rules require clear #ad disclosure of paid and affiliate content

stated_problem.quote: If you're inside one of these tech companies and your AI bill is going through the roof

idea.name: OpenRouter – LLM task router
idea.one_liner: An API that sends each task to the cheapest model that can handle it (open source vs frontier), cutting companies' AI bills.
idea.offer: One routing layer across many models

key_quotes.quote: open router, which is a tool for you send a task to it and open router will decide, let's let's use a cheap, you know, open source model for this.
open router's data shows that more and more tasks don't require Einstein, they just need the intern.
Wait, every company in the world's going to have this problem and then you build the company off it.

claims.claim: Valued at nearly $10B (stated as a question)
claims.quote: Do they, they sell for 10 billion nearly?

claims.claim: Raised only about $150M
claims.quote: I don't know. Only 150 million.

ideas.delivery: API software routing between hosted models
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR (data processor for routed prompts)

idea.name: AI Tamagotchi-style companion app
idea.one_liner: A consumer app with a cute AI animal companion that messages users first, takes an interest in them and keeps them engaged.
idea.offer: An AI companion chat (it asks for selfies, chats about hobbies)

key_quotes.quote: who's created a AI, like fuzzy, like bare, like a little animal, Tamagotchi type of thing that you can chat with.
wow, this thing takes a lot of interest in me.

claims.claim: Close to a $100M run rate
claims.quote: And I think they're on like a almost $100 million run rate or something.

claims.claim: Tens of millions run rate, maybe near $100M
claims.quote: It's in the tens of millions if not getting close to $100 million run rate.

ideas.delivery: A mobile app with an AI chat companion
ideas.other_uk_rules: Online Safety Act 2023 (child safety for chatbots), UK GDPR (images and personal data), DMCC Act subscription rules

stated_problem.quote: Rich people used to have private drivers and black cars that would, they would tell them, hey, I'm ready.

idea.name: Uber – on-demand rides
idea.one_liner: Gives everyone the private driver that only the rich used to have, with on-demand rides from an app.

key_quotes.quote: But this idea that you take what was always available for the ultra wealthy if you make it available to everybody.

ideas.other_uk_rules: Private hire licensing (TfL); worker status rules

idea.name: Sidecar – early rideshare
idea.one_liner: A rideshare app that came before Uber; it was beaten as competition intensified.

key_quotes.quote: And then it got smashed very quickly because the race intensified and got so competitive so fast.

stated_problem.quote: The ultra wealthy, wealthy had vacation homes.

idea.name: Airbnb – vacation homes for everyone
idea.one_liner: Makes stays in vacation homes available to everyone through a host marketplace.

ideas.delivery: Hosts provide the homes; the platform matches guests to them

idea.name: DoorDash – aggregator charging both sides
idea.one_liner: A food delivery aggregator that charges customers fees and also charges restaurants for orders it sends them.
idea.revenue_model: Customer service fees plus merchant commission

key_quotes.quote: They also charge the restaurant because they're like, they're telling the restaurant, hey, you wouldn't have had this order if it wasn't for us.
there's too much power in the hands of this aggregator in the middle.
